data_output.description: data.py remains unchanged. encode(splits) returns (encoded, dimension), where each split is (features, labels, users); features is an int32 array of shape (n, 2), with encoded user ID in column 0 and encoded video ID in column 1, in canonical split row order. Training must not load ground truth outside the labels already supplied by data.py, and must not reorder validation rows.

model_input.description: model.py must retain Model(dimension, learning_rate=0.01, l2=1e-6), logits(features), step(features, labels), predict(features, batch_size=200000), state(), and load_state(state). For each row, derive a deterministic hash bucket from the two encoded feature IDs using a stable integer hash, modulo 262144; never use Python's randomized hash. Compute logits as the existing additive-plus-16-dimensional interaction score plus cross_weights[bucket]. Initialize cross_weights to zeros, apply the configured l2 penalty to it through the same Adam update path, and include its first/second moments and values in state checkpoints. Preserve finite 1-D predictions and empty-input behavior.
